reason: The cited evidence directly supports the feasibility of forming a metastable W(Cu) solid solution via Cu coating and CPF treatment, the quenching rates, and the improved radiation resistance, but the specific claim of 'ultra-thin, uniform copper layer' via vapor deposition is not explicitly described in the cited passages, and the quantitative link to enhanced thermal transport and mechanical durability under fusion conditions is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
premises: W and Cu are immiscible under equilibrium, requiring non-equilibrium methods to form a metastable solid solution
Pulsed compression plasma flow (CPF) treatment can produce cooling rates of 10^6–10^7 K/s, enabling quenching effects
CPF treatment of Cu-coated W can form a W(Cu) solid solution, evidenced by a decrease in W lattice parameter
CPF pre-treatment of W creates a finely dispersed structure that increases radiation resistance under He ion irradiation
Vapor deposition can provide a uniform Cu coating on W surfaces prior to CPF treatment
